FIXED THE ACTUAL CAUSE of "Record Audio never fills in the audio path." v307/v308/v309 each
patched the polling AROUND this and never the source it polls. The app was asking the DEPLOYED
WEBSITE for data.json to find out whether narration finished. But the Action commits data.json
and the audio file to GitHub, where both exist immediately, while the deployed site can lag a
push by a minute or more — and the workflow's own commit message carries "[skip ci]", so that
push may not trigger a redeploy at all. So the app could poll forever for something already
sitting in the repo the whole time, then correctly report "gave up." It now reads data.json
straight from the GitHub contents API on the configured branch, which reflects the Action's
commit the instant it lands. The deployed data.json is kept only as a fallback for when GitHub
isn't configured or reachable, so nothing changes for that case.
The v309 auto-detect check had the identical flaw — it HEAD-checked the live site for a file
GitHub already had. It now asks GitHub first (contents API: 200 = in the repo, 404 = not),
falling back to the site only when the API can't give a definite answer. An inconclusive API
response (rate limit, auth) never counts as "file missing."
v309 (unchanged): Manage → Entries auto-fills a blank audio field when a file already exists at
the conventional audio/<Category>/<id>-v<N>.mp3 path. Save Entry still needed to keep it.
v308 (unchanged): syncAudioStatusUntilFresh always writes a final message on both the success
and give-up paths instead of leaving stale "attempt N/max" text frozen on screen.
v307 (unchanged): triggerWorkflow/syncAudioStatusUntilFresh take an attempt-count override so
Record Audio can wait minutes (a real batch) rather than the seconds Resize/Convert need.
Manage → Entries editor now auto-detects audio that already exists but never made it into the
`audio` field. Opening an entry whose audio field is blank quietly HEAD-checks the conventional
path (audio/<Category>/<id>-v<N>.mp3, falling back to .wav for anything recorded before the
mp3 switch, and walking versions upward since nextVersion() never leaves a gap) using the exact
same folder-per-type naming generate-audio.mjs writes to. A hit fills the field in immediately
(and the status bar says so) — Save Entry still needed to keep it, same as any other edit. A
miss is silent; this is a courtesy check, not a requirement. Covers exactly the gap the v308
fix was about: a file that made it to the repo/site but whose data.json field never caught up.
v308 (unchanged, kept for reference): fixed Record Audio looking permanently "stuck" even when
the sync actually succeeded — syncAudioStatusUntilFresh now always writes a final message on
both the success and give-up exit paths instead of leaving stale "attempt N/max" text on screen.
v307 (unchanged, kept for reference): fixed Record Audio never picking up its own results
automatically — triggerWorkflow/syncAudioStatusUntilFresh were tuned for Resize/Convert
(finish in seconds), not a real audio batch (minutes); both now take an attempt-count override
and Record Audio budgets patience scaled to batch size.
Fixed Record Audio never picking up its own results automatically. The client-side polling
that watches for a workflow to finish (triggerWorkflow) and then waits for data.json to catch
up (syncAudioStatusUntilFresh) both existed already, but were tuned for Resize Images/Convert
Photos, which finish in seconds — ~60s total patience between the two. A real audio batch needs
a separate ElevenLabs call per section (heading + body) plus ffmpeg work per entry, so it can
genuinely take minutes, not seconds; the client was giving up long before the server had
anything to report, which is why the audio field never seemed to arrive on its own. Both
functions now take an optional attempt-count override — Resize/Convert are untouched and still
give up after ~60s, but Record Audio now budgets roughly 3 minutes of "is it done yet" patience
per entry, plus ~80s per entry of deploy-lag margin after that, scaled to the actual batch size.
Status text while waiting is now honest about what's happening ("narration can take several
minutes for a full batch") instead of implying a fast deploy-lag hiccup.

"card" when something is visible beside it; nothing is now. Still slides in from the left.
Status column reduced from an 84px word to a 26px glyph, no header label: ○ queued,
◐ running, ● waiting on you, ✓ done/approved, ✕ rejected (grey) or error (red). Every pixel
it gave up went to the Task column, which is the one carrying text that has to be readable;
Task rows also went to 15px.
Status sorting and its sticky grouping REMOVED rather than kept as an unlabelled tap target:
the All/Queued/Review chips already do status filtering, so a status sort was a second way
to do the same thing. Sort is now Task or Date.
Batch controls beside Run: a count box (1–50) and a service dropdown. They are the run's
arguments — "do 5 of these" — and become workflow_dispatch inputs. Both service dropdowns
(Run and Add Task) build from one TK_SERVICES array so they can't drift apart.
Backend: orchestrator.mjs takes a TASK_TYPE filter, and orchestrator.yml gains a matching
task_type input.
Backend: running out of budget is now a first-class outcome distinct from failure. A handler
returning {deferred:true, reason} — or throwing an error with .deferred — puts its task back
to `queued` exactly as it was, stops the rest of the batch (the budget is gone; retrying each
one would fail identically), and writes a plain-language `notice` onto workLog.json. Nothing
turns red, nothing is lost, and the items are simply picked up next run. The panel shows that
notice in an amber banner above the list. Verified end to end with a deferring test handler:
3 tasks in, 3 still queued, no errors, notice written.
Step 1 of the task-pipeline UI plan. Reshaped #taskPanel around two tabs — Add Task and
Task List — plus a third view (Review) reached by tapping a review item rather than by a
tab of its own, because reviewing is a drill-down, not a peer destination.
Review is now a QUEUE you work through, not a detail pane you browse. Tapping a proposal
opens that item full-panel; Approve or Reject both advance straight to the next proposal
with no confirmation step; the last one returns to the list. Queue order is oldest-first by
createdAt (timestamp order), captured when review opens so a run landing mid-review can't
reshuffle what you're partway through.
The review view renders the ENTRY the task would change — Quick Facts and article — with a
gold bar (.tkTarget) down the left edge of the row or paragraph being touched, the
light-theme counterpart of the audio narration's white .audioActiveBar. Drawn as a
positioned ::before rather than a border so marking a row never shifts its layout. The
marked row shows the proposed NEW value in place; the old value is deliberately not shown.
Target address comes from the task's own patch (["facts","Died","U",…]) and is resolved the
same two ways applyOnePatch() accepts (label or 1-based position), so the marker always
lands where the edit actually will, with nothing hardcoded per service. Handles U/I/D on
facts and article text; a task with no entity or no patch (a scan, a failure) falls back to
the plain summary card, which is also what a finished task opens as, read-only.
Locked bottom section (.tkLockBar, flex:0 0 auto) holds the review options and never moves
no matter how long the entry above it runs: Approve · Reject, a position counter, and the
follow-up checkbox slot.
"Record audio" checkbox implemented per the agreed rule — offered only when the task created
a whole entry AND that entry has no audio yet. Rendered DISABLED with the reason stated:
the orchestrator has no TTS handler yet (Step 3), so ticking it would queue work nothing
runs. Shown rather than hidden so the shape of the step is visible.
Chips reduced to All · Queued · Review. Queued deliberately includes in_progress — a running
task is still work you're waiting on. Finished items have no chip; they live under All, greyed.
X means "back to list" while reviewing and "close panel" everywhere else.
Manage → Work tab REMOVED entirely; the Add Task form moved into the panel, so the whole
loop now lives in one place. Its markup, handler, and remaining .wl* CSS deleted rather than
left as a second way in.
Reworked the v272 Work tab into "Task : Automation" (#taskPanel), a left-sliding panel built
on the SAME shell as the Saints/Browse panels — .panelHead/.spHead/.spCol/.spListWrap/.spList/
.spRow chrome, same z-index band, same .48s transition, same scrim mechanics. Opened from
☰ → Owner Tools → Task : Automation.
Three sortable columns in the fixed|flex|fixed shape the other two panels already use:
Status (84px) | Task (flexible) | Date (78px). Date is the default, newest first, since a
work log reads as a running history. Sorting by Status groups the list under sticky status
headers via the existing groupStickyRows() — same rule Browse applies to Region/Country:
grouping only when actually sorted by that column.
Row colour carries state, per the ask: finished work (done/approved/rejected) greys out
(.tkFinished), anything still live (queued/in_progress/proposed) stays black, so what's left
to do is what the eye lands on. The Status cell itself is colour-coded — amber = waiting to
run, blue = waiting on you, green = settled, red = broken.
Status sort order is deliberately NOT alphabetical (TK_STATUS_ORDER): proposed first, since
it's the only state waiting on a human, then queued/in_progress, then error, then settled.
New detail pane (.tkDetail) pinned beneath the list, its own scroll, filled by tapping a row
(tapping the same row again clears it). Renders from whatever the task actually carries:
oldDied/newDied become a struck-through before/after; a scan result becomes a readable
sentence ("Checked 224 saints. 0 qualified…" plus the skip reasons spelled out) — this closes
the v272 gap where a completed scan's summary was only legible by opening the raw JSON on
GitHub; an error shows its text; anything else falls back to pretty-printed JSON so a service
written later is reviewable before it has a custom renderer.
Approve/Reject live in the detail pane, with "Approve all N" when the proposal has batch
siblings. Batch approve still only touches items at "proposed", so it can't override a reject.
Filter chips: All · Review · Active · Finished, reusing .spChips/.spChip.
Refresh + Run moved into the panel's top bar; wlSetLog() now writes to the panel's count line.
Manage → Work reduced to the Add-a-Task form (queuing a task is an owner action and belongs in
the CMS); its list/review markup, listeners, and ~3.6KB of now-dead .wl* CSS removed rather
than left to rot as a second, competing view of the same data.
NEW "Work" tab (6th CMS tab) — the in-app half of the orchestrator content pipeline whose
backend (workLog.json, scripts/orchestrator.mjs, scripts/services/age-backfill.mjs,
.github/workflows/orchestrator.yml) now lives in the repo. Three sections:
• Work Log — Refresh reads workLog.json straight from the GitHub API (same owner/repo/
branch/token fields as Publish, nothing new to configure); Run Orchestrator fires the
workflow via the existing triggerWorkflow() and re-reads the file when it finishes.
• Add a Task — queues one task and commits it immediately. The immediate commit is not
an oversight: the Action runs on GitHub and can only see what is actually in the repo,
so a task held in browser memory would be invisible to it. Two write rhythms on
purpose — workLog.json writes fast and often, data.json still only moves on Publish.
• Review Queue — one card per "proposed" task, grouped by the batch that spawned it,
with Approve/Reject per card plus "Approve All N" on the batch header. Batch approve
only ever touches items still sitting at "proposed", so it can never override a
reject already made on an individual card.
Approving applies the task's patch through the SAME applyOnePatch() the Paste JSON importer
uses — one code path for "a patch is applied to an entry" regardless of whether it arrived
by clipboard or by service — then saveDb()/render()/renderMList(), and re-opens the editor
if the patched entry is the one currently open (the v240 stale-form guard: without it,
"Save, Publish & Exit" writes the pre-approval form back over the change).
Approve merges into this session only. Content reaches the live site through the existing
Publish to GitHub button, so there is still exactly one publish gate for all content.
saveWorkLog() re-reads the blob sha before every PUT and, if the remote moved since load,
merges task rows by id rather than replacing the file wholesale — the Action committing its
own run in between is the normal case here, not an edge case.
Review cards render from the task's own result: oldDied/newDied produce a struck-through
before/after pair; anything else falls back to pretty-printed JSON, so a service added later
is reviewable before its custom renderer exists.
Removed the drag-thumb scrub bubble's stem and moved the bubble down half a row instead.
The stem could not be made to work: the label is positioned ~90px above the fingertip on
purpose (so a thumb doesn't cover the row it names), while the thumb rail sits off to its
right — from that offset no tail direction actually reaches the thumb, so v268's nudge and
any further nudge would still read as broken rather than as a comic word-bubble tail. Dropped
`.spThumbLabel::after` entirely and changed the vertical offset from -90 to -69 (90 less half
of --rowH's 43px) in both drag handlers, landing the bubble nearer the row it names while
still clearing the finger. Both the Saints panel and the generic Browse panel share the
.spThumbLabel styling, so both offsets were changed together to keep the two in step.
Fixed the real bug behind "text not found" on any `patches` `article` match text that touched
an HTML tag, even a fully-balanced one (e.g. `Michael`) — every such patch was silently
unmatchable, not just theoretically restricted. patchTextInSections() previously split each
section's body into tag-separated pieces first (`sec.b.split(/(<[^>]+>)/g)`), then searched
each piece alone — so match text spanning a tag could never be found in any single piece,
regardless of whether the source text matched perfectly. That tokenizing existed to stop a
patch from partially matching into an `<a href="entry:...">` cross-reference link's visible
text (which could silently break navigation), a real protection worth keeping — it just also,
as a side effect, caught every other tag along with it. Rewrote to match against each section's
full raw body directly, then reject only matches that actually overlap an `...` span
(full or partial), via a precomputed list of anchor ranges — same protection, without the
accidental blast radius. `patches` `article` matches can now include `<b>`/`<i>`/etc. markup
same as the skill doc always described. See json-import-skill.md Part 2 — no format change,
this was purely an app-side matching bug.
Drag-thumb scrub bubble (.spThumbLabel, shared by the Saints panel and every generic Browse
panel — Councils, Persecutions, Eucharistic, Events, Marian) — the stem pointing from the
bubble down to the gold thumb fell short of it, reading as disconnected rather than a comic
word-bubble tail actually touching its target. Shifted the stem's ::after triangle right and
down (right:12px->-3px, bottom:-7px->-22px, ~15px each direction) so its tip lands on the
thumb's rail.
Record Audio Narration (Manage → Import) now records by feast day: with Category set to
Saint, the Start field switches from a year to a month/day ("Aug 15" or "8/15"), the pool
sorts by feast date (earliest date per saint, via the existing parseFeastDates()/entryFeastDates())
instead of year, and the Start/Will-record preview lines show the feast date instead of the
year. Every other category is unchanged — still year-based, oldest first. New
updateAudioStartFieldMode() swaps the field's label/type/placeholder on category change and on
Manage open (audioCategory is restored from localStorage, so it may already be 's' on open).
Export tab: new "Feast Day (Saints only)" range row below Years, taking the same month/day
text format ("Aug 15") as the audio tool above and sharing its parseMonthDay()/feastInRange()
helpers, including calendar wraparound (Dec 26 – Jan 2). Only narrows Saints — every other
category passes through untouched — so it can ride alongside the existing category/region/
status/year filters. Feeds mExportFilteredEntries(), so it applies consistently across
JSON — Filtered, Excel, CSV-fallback export, and the cross-reference scan/apply tools, same as
every other Export filter. Reset now also clears both new fields.
